name: Diabetes
overview: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic condition where blood glucose stays elevated because the body cannot produce enough insulin or use it effectively. India has one of the world's largest diabetic populations. Early diagnosis and sustained control reduce complications affecting the eyes, kidneys, nerves, and heart.
symptoms: Tingling or numbness in feet (long-standing disease)
causes: Type 1: autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
Type 2: insulin resistance plus progressive beta-cell failure
Secondary causes: pancreatitis, certain medicines, endocrine disorders
riskFactors: South Asian ethnicity (higher risk at lower BMI)
diagnosis: Oral glucose tolerance test when indicated
Urine albumin and kidney function tests
Lipid profile and blood pressure monitoring
treatment: Lifestyle modification: diet, exercise, weight management
Metformin as first-line in most type 2 diabetes
Additional agents (SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 agonists, insulin) as needed
Foot care and self-monitoring of glucose
prevention: Maintain healthy weight and regular physical activity
Balanced diet low in refined carbohydrates
Screen adults with risk factors every 1–3 years
Manage prediabetes with structured lifestyle programmes
emergencySigns: Severe hypoglycaemia with sweating and shakiness
Non-healing foot wound with fever or spreading redness

faq.question: Can I rely on this Diabetes information instead of a doctor visit?
faq.answer: No. This content supports learning and preparation for conversations with qualified healthcare professionals. It is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment.

faq.question: What should I do if Diabetes symptoms worsen suddenly?
faq.answer: Seek urgent medical care, especially if severe pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or high fever develops.
